Replies.Text:
Where the Server window loads its page from. Today it loads the Server's own address (http://127.0.0.1:<port>/) as a browser would, and its preload adds window.ConsensusServer for the sign-in and window.Desktop.PickFolder. The other three windows load the page from electron/Page.js on a loopback origin of their own, with the Server's API forwarded under /servers/<key>/api, and their preload gives the full ConsensusDesktop bridge (the look, the remembered state, the chrome message, the close asked of the page, Print to PDF and View in Browser).

The two ways: (a) keep loading the Server's address and give the window the full bridge anyway: the frameless window works, but ViewInBrowser (which maps a report's address from the page server's root back to the server's) has nothing to map and needs a Server-only path, and the window's origin changes with the Server's port; (b) load the page through the page server with one root, Key server, as the plan says: every edition's window then has the same shape and the same bridge, ViewInBrowser works as it does for the others, and the sign-in keeps working since the forwarder sends X-Forwarded-Host, which Api.js honours over the loopback. The cost is a second loopback listener in the Server process (the page server), which the other three already pay.

Recommendation: (b), the page server, as the plan says. The page server's port is remembered in server.json as page-port (App.ServePage), so the window's origin, and the Clerk session in its storage, survive a restart. Resolve with no reply to take it.
